source_text: II. Martianus ait: Responde, cui deo precem fundis? ut ipsi etiam nos sacra reddamus. Achatius dixit: Ego deum meum opto te scire quod prosit et deum qui est verus agnoscere. Martianus ait: Nomen eius mihi enuntia. Achatius dixit: Deus Abraham, deus Isaac et deus Iacob. Martianus ait: Deorum ista sunt nomina? Achatius respondit: Non isti, sed qui locutus est istis, ille est deus verus, illum timere debemus. Martianus ait: Quis est iste? respondit Achatius: Altissimus Adonai, sedens super cherubim et seraphim. Martianus ait: Quid est seraphim? cui Achatius: Altissimi dei minister et excelsae sedis antistes.
pass_a_gloss: Martianus says: Give answer, to which god you pour forth entreaty, in order that we also may render holy offerings to him in person. Achatius said: I wish you to come to know my god, for what may do good, and to acknowledge the god who is genuine. Martianus says: Pronounce his name for me. Achatius said: God of Abraham, god of Isaac and god of Jacob. Martianus says: Are those things names of gods? Achatius answered: Not those men, but the one who spoke to them, that one is the genuine god, that one we ought to fear. Martianus says: Who is that one? Achatius answered: Highest Adonai, seated over cherubim and seraphim. Martianus says: What is seraphim? To him Achatius: An attendant of the highest god and a minister of the elevated seat.
pass_b_english: Martianus said: Answer me, to which god do you pour out your prayer, so that we too may offer worship to him in person?
Achatius said: I want you to know my God, for your own good, and to acknowledge the God who is true.
Martianus said: Speak his name to me.
Achatius said: The God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.
Martianus said: Are those the names of gods?
Achatius answered: Not those men, but the one who spoke to them, he is the true God, and him we must fear.
Achatius answered: The Most High Adonai, enthroned above the cherubim and the seraphim.
Achatius said to him: A servant of the Most High God and a high priest of the exalted throne.

choices.why: fundis with precem as direct object keeps the liquid-pouring metaphor for uttering prayer, rather than a generic verb for praying
reddare sacra with dative ipsi is cultic payment of due rites to the same god, not private prayer alone
sedens super with heavenly beings denotes enthronement in biblical idiom, not merely sitting in a place
